summary.en: El Salvador has deployed elite forces to Haiti to rescue four kidnapped aviation technicians and four Salvadoran soldiers held by Haitian gangs, and President Bukele has warned the gangs of a harsh response to further attacks. The gangs have abducted the Salvadoran personnel in an ambush, prompting the rescue mission. This operation adds a direct foreign military intervention to the ongoing gang-state conflict in Port-au-Prince. The conflict produced 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: El Salvador har sendt inn elite-styrker til Haiti for å redde fire kidnappede luftfartsteknikere og fire salvadoranske soldater som holdes av haitiske gjenger, og president Bukele har advart gjengene om en hard respons på ytterligere angrep. Gjengene har bortført det salvadoranske personellet i et bakholdsangrep, noe som har ført til redningsoperasjonen. Denne operasjonen tilfører en direkte utenlandsk militær intervensjon til den pågående gjeng-stat-konflikten i Port-au-Prince. Konflikten har forårsaket 193 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
